snips.text: So, we are driving through the desert
right now. I need to get to Dubai.
Riyadh Airport is closed and we figured
out the shortest route is to drive to
Bahrain and then fly to Dubai with my
colleague Muhammad over here,
who is driving.
And this is the
scenery.
More and more people are taking the land
route out of Saudi Arabia after Houthi
attacks on the airports, on the Riyadh
airport, on Dammam, and on others in the
south of the country.
And that's a big shift from what we saw
earlier on in the war where Saudi Arabia
became sort of the haven for people
fleeing Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait when they
were facing the brunt of Iranian
attacks. That map has now flipped and
embassies and companies are recommending
that their that their citizens and their
employees actually go to neighboring
Gulf states and fly from there.
That's a sign of just how much the war
has come home
to the kingdom. I mean, the Yemen war is
an old one. Saudi Arabia got involved 12
years ago.
And at the time, they had similar goals
that the Yemeni government have now,
which was to push the Houthis back
into the mountains, out of the capital.
It hasn't worked for 12 years and many
people are skeptical of the current
campaign and its ability to affect a
change on the ground. There are several
routes that people are using out of the
kingdom now.
I'm currently driving to Bahrain, which
is about a four or five-hour drive. You
can also go the land route to Qatar,
which is seven or eight hours, or drive
to the Emirates,
you know, to Abu Dhabi, it's about
seven or eight. To Dubai, you can add on
another two or three hours to that.
Life is, of course, in many ways it's on
as normal.
People go to work. Um you know, you see
people out and about in the streets.
But there has been an impact. Um
schools have been doing uh learning from
home for
about a couple of weeks now. Um a lot of
offices in some of the key areas in the
capital also uh are are working from
home. Um so you you certainly do feel
something. And of course, the the events
calendar that usually really picks up uh
in the autumn in Saudi Arabia and across
the Gulf has been severely impacted.
Everything from tennis to racing
um to fashion week to music festivals,
many of these things that have appeared
in the kingdom just in the past 5 to 10
years
uh are now called off.

meta.title: On the road to Bahrain as Houthi attacks hit Saudi Arabia's haven status
meta.author: Reuters
